title: DR1's 'Help with commodity codes' explains what a commodity code is and links out to the Trade Tariff tool to look one up; the frontend's opens on a single sentence and no link.

finding.frontend: The page has the details component and the same summary text, so the difference is what is inside it. Expanded, it reads 'Commodity codes are used to classify goods for import and export.' and nothing else — one sentence, no link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:7-10, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:31-34). A user who does not know their commodity code is left where they started.
finding.prototype: DR1's details holds three paragraphs: 'Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.', 'A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.', and 'You can look up commodity codes using the Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab).' — the last carrying a link to https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff that opens in a new tab (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:119-131).
finding.difference: Replace the one-sentence help text with DR1's three paragraphs and add the Trade Tariff link, marked as opening in a new tab. The copy string becomes HTML rather than plain text, so the details call in the search template takes html instead of text.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a link to the Trade Tariff tool anywhere on the frontend's What are you importing? page.
